topic: 综合模拟二与稳定性检查 · Independent new scenario: public decisions when evidence is incomplete
grammarFocus: 根据两轮结果检查重复错误，巩固准确表达与稳定句型。 Teach the new rule in Chinese, then provide at least 8 distinct grammar questions in new sentences. Distinguish a newly taught form from revision. All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. Preserve a coherent new scenario; do not rename an earlier text, reuse its facts or reveal answers in question stems.
sourcePolicy: Project-original scenario; simulated figures and people; no copied official test, textbook, GitHub PDF or third-party audio.
title: The Library Roof Decision
instructions: 项目原创模拟场景与数据，不是官方试卷。阅读文章后独立回答10题，再检查逐题依据。题目包含信息定位、论证范围、比较及推断；遇到词汇可用划词帮助，但使用帮助不算独立测评。语法先看规则，再做新语境练习。
passage:
A. The town of Marlow Vale faced a problem. Its public library, a small brick building on King Street, had a leaking roof. Rain had damaged books and computers. The town council had to decide whether to repair the roof or move the library to a larger building near the train station. The council had a budget of £120,000. The repair would cost about £80,000. Moving would cost £150,000, but the new building would be bigger and easier to reach. The council asked the town's residents for their opinions. Exactly 1,620 adults answered an online survey. Most of them said they wanted a bigger library. However, only 18 percent of the town's 9,000 adults completed the survey. The council knew that this was not a perfect picture of public opinion. The low response rate meant that the survey results might not represent the views of the whole community. For example, people who did not use the library or who were too busy might not have taken part. Therefore, the council decided to gather more information before making a final decision.

B. The council held two public meetings. At the first meeting, many older residents said they liked the current library because it was close to their homes. They did not want to walk to the station. They also said that the library was a familiar place where they felt comfortable. At the second meeting, younger residents and parents said the library was too small for children's activities. They wanted more space. One parent said, “We need a place where kids can read and play.” A local business owner offered to give £20,000 to help with the move. But he also said the council should wait for more information. The council's finance officer warned that repair costs might rise. She said, “The roof is old. We may find more problems when we start work.” She explained that old buildings often have hidden damage, such as weak walls or outdated wiring, which could increase the total cost. The council therefore needed to be careful with its limited budget.

C. The council decided to take a middle path. They voted to repair the roof first, using £80,000. They also agreed to spend £10,000 on a study about moving the library in the future. The study will look at costs, parking, and bus routes. It will also consider how many people use the library and what services they need. The council will receive the study results in six months. The remaining £30,000 will be kept for emergencies. The council leader explained, “We are not saying no to a new library. We are saying we need better evidence before we spend a large amount of money.” Some residents were unhappy. They said the council was too slow. Others were pleased. They said the council was careful with public money. The leader added that the council would consider all options once the study was complete.

D. The library will stay open during the roof repair. However, the children's reading room will be closed for three weeks. The council will put a temporary reading area in the town hall. The library staff will move 2,000 children's books to the town hall. The repair work will start on 15 March and finish by 30 April. The council has promised to hold another public meeting in May to discuss interim questions and the future of the library; the completed six-month study would not yet be available. The town's newspaper, the Marlow Vale Gazette, will report on the meeting. The council also said it would put all documents online so that residents can read them. This includes the survey results, the study report, and the cost estimates. The leader added, “We want people to see the facts. Then we can make a better decision together.” The council hopes that more residents will take part in the discussion this time. To encourage this, the council plans to advertise the meeting on its website and in local shops, and to provide a summary of the documents in plain language. The leader stressed that the emergency repair work would not affect the library's opening hours, except for the children's room. He also thanked the residents who had already shared their views and urged others to get involved.

E. The finance officer proposed comparing the options over ten years rather than judging them by their initial prices alone. Repairing the roof might be cheaper immediately but leave expensive maintenance later; relocation might have higher initial costs but lower running costs. Neither possibility had yet been quantified. The study would therefore present several scenarios instead of one apparently precise forecast. It would state assumptions about energy prices, building condition and expected use, and show how conclusions changed when those assumptions changed. The officer also warned against treating the possible business donation as money already available. A promise conditional on a move could not finance a decision to stay. Keeping an emergency reserve reduced the risk of abandoning essential work halfway through, although it left less money for other services. The council accepted that choosing a cautious sequence still had an opportunity cost: residents would wait longer for any extra space. Evidence could make that trade-off clearer, but could not remove the need to choose.

questions.prompt: What was the council's budget for the library problem?
questions.explanation: 文章第一段明确说“The council had a budget of £120,000.”，因此预算是12万英镑。
questions.evidence: The council had a budget of £120,000.

questions.prompt: Why was an eighteen-percent response rate not sufficient by itself to establish what all adults wanted?
options: Those who responded might differ systematically from those who did not.
The survey showed that every adult used the library.
A response rate directly establishes the cost of moving.
The respondents were stated to be a random sample of all adults.
answers: Those who responded might differ systematically from those who did not.
questions.explanation: 低回复率本身不自动证明偏差，但未回复者可能是不用图书馆或太忙的人，意见可能不同，所以不能只凭比例断定全体意见。原文没有随机抽样保证。
questions.evidence: For example, people who did not use the library or who were too busy might not have taken part.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of paragraph B?
options: To show competing access needs and uncertainty about the financial options.
To establish that every resident preferred relocation.
To show that the business donation removed all financial risk.
To report the completed study's final recommendation.
answers: To show competing access needs and uncertainty about the financial options.
questions.explanation: 老人重视旧址近，年轻家庭需要空间，同时有维修超支风险与搬迁捐款条件；本段没有一致赞成、零风险或已完成研究结论。
questions.evidence: At the first meeting, many older residents said they liked the current library because it was close to their homes. They did not want to walk to the station. They also said that the library was a familiar place where they felt comfortable. At the second meeting, younger residents and parents said the library was too small for children's activities. They wanted more space. One parent said, “We need a place where kids can read and play.” A local business owner offered to give £20,000 to help with the move. But he also said the council should wait for more information. The council's finance officer warned that repair costs might rise.

questions.prompt: The council voted to repair the roof first.
questions.explanation: C段明确说“They voted to repair the roof first, using £80,000.”，因此该陈述为真。
questions.evidence: They voted to repair the roof first, using £80,000.

questions.prompt: Which interpretation of the phased decision is supported?
options: It addresses urgent damage while leaving the longer-term location decision open.
It guarantees relocation as soon as the roof has been repaired.
It establishes that repairing has the lowest total cost over ten years.
It rejects the need for further evidence about access and costs.
answers: It addresses urgent damage while leaving the longer-term location decision open.
questions.explanation: 先修紧急损坏并研究未来搬迁，保留后续选择；尚未承诺搬迁，也未完成十年成本比较。
questions.evidence: We are not saying no to a new library. We are saying we need better evidence before we spend a large amount of money.

questions.prompt: Decide whether the statement agrees with the passage: The business owner who offered a donation owned two shops in the town.
questions.explanation: 原文说一位当地企业主提出捐款，没有说明其企业或店铺数量；“business owner”不能推出恰好一家或两家店，所以数量信息未给出。
questions.evidence: A local business owner offered to give £20,000 to help with the move.

questions.prompt: The children's reading room will be closed for ______ weeks. (Use one word from the passage.)
questions.explanation: D段说“the children's reading room will be closed for three weeks.”，因此填three。
questions.evidence: the children's reading room will be closed for three weeks.

questions.prompt: The repair work will start on ______. (Use ONE WORD AND A NUMBER from the passage.)
questions.explanation: D段说“The repair work will start on 15 March and finish by 30 April.”，因此开始日期是15 March。
questions.evidence: The repair work will start on 15 March and finish by 30 April.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of varying assumptions in the ten-year study?
options: To show how dependent the recommendation is on uncertain future conditions.
To guarantee a single forecast will be exactly correct.
To ignore future maintenance in favour of the cheapest initial price.
To count a conditional donation as cash already received.
answers: To show how dependent the recommendation is on uncertain future conditions.
questions.explanation: 改变假设检验结论是否稳健；不是精确预测保证，也不是忽视维护或提前确认附条件捐款。
questions.evidence: It would state assumptions about energy prices, building condition and expected use, and show how conclusions changed when those assumptions changed.

questions.prompt: What limitation of the cautious sequence is acknowledged?
options: Waiting for evidence delays any additional space and still involves a trade-off.
It makes urgent roof work impossible.
It eliminates the need to compare services competing for funds.
It ensures the conditional donation can pay for staying in the old building.
answers: Waiting for evidence delays any additional space and still involves a trade-off.
questions.explanation: 谨慎决策也有机会成本：扩容延迟，其他服务可用钱减少；证据使取舍更清楚，无法取消取舍。其余选项与先维修、保留备用金和条件捐款不符。
questions.evidence: The council accepted that choosing a cautious sequence still had an opportunity cost: residents would wait longer for any extra space.

grammar.title: 可能性、过去推断与条件捐款：避免把计划写成既成事实
grammar.explanation: may/might +动词原形表示可能，不保证结果；两者强弱取决于语境，不能机械按固定概率排序。may/might have +过去分词表示对过去的可能推断，may have been +过去分词则兼有被动意义。条件句only if表示必要条件；条件尚未满足不能把承诺写成已到账。修饰costs的分词短语或关系从句要区分预计、承诺与已经发生。
grammar.example: We may find more problems when we start work.

questions.prompt: The weather is cloudy. It ______ rain later.
questions.explanation: may 后接动词原形，不随主语变化，也不加 to 或 -ing。因此选 may。
questions.evidence: We may find more problems when we start work.

questions.prompt: A payment was possibly delayed yesterday; this is not yet confirmed. The payment ___ by the bank.
questions.explanation: 过去可能发生的被动事件用 might have been delayed。might delay tomorrow 改成将来；must have delayed 缺少这里需要的被动结构且推断过强；cannot have been delayed 则排除了可能。
questions.evidence: A payment was possibly delayed yesterday; this is not yet confirmed. The payment might have been delayed by the bank.

options: The train may to arrive late.
questions.explanation: 情态动词 may 不随主语变化，后接动词原形 arrive，因此正确句为 The train may arrive late。
questions.evidence: We may find more problems when we start work.

questions.prompt: We are not sure about the cost. The repair ______ more than £80,000.
questions.explanation: might 后接动词原形 cost，表示不确定的可能性。因此选 might cost。
questions.evidence: We may find more problems when we start work.

questions.prompt: The donor will pay only on condition that the library moves. Preserve that necessary condition: The donor will pay ___ the library moves.
questions.explanation: only if保留“搬迁是付款必要条件”；even if和whether or not弱化或取消条件，as though表示仿佛。
questions.evidence: The donor will pay only on condition that the library moves. Preserve that necessary condition: The donor will pay only if the library moves.

questions.prompt: The council ______ not have enough money for a new building.
questions.explanation: may not + 动词原形表示“可能不”。may 不随主语变化，因此选 may。
questions.evidence: We may find more problems when we start work.

questions.prompt: Refer to costs that have not yet been confirmed: The costs ___ in the preliminary report are estimates, not invoices.
questions.explanation: projected作过去分词后置修饰costs，相当于that are projected；完整谓语或多余宾语会破坏这里的主句结构。估计不等于已收到账单。
questions.evidence: Refer to costs that have not yet been confirmed: The costs projected in the preliminary report are estimates, not invoices.

questions.prompt: Express that the move remains merely possible: The committee said the library ___ move after the review, but no decision had been made.
questions.explanation: might保留尚未决定的可能性；must definitely写成必然，had already写成已发生（且后应moved），cannot possibly排除可能，均改变意思。
questions.evidence: Express that the move remains merely possible: The committee said the library might move after the review, but no decision had been made.

part1: What do you think makes a good public library?
Have you ever taken part in a public meeting or survey?
Do you prefer to make decisions quickly or slowly?
speaking.part2: Describe a time when a group had to make a decision with incomplete information. You should say: what the decision was; who was involved; what information was missing; and what the result was.
part3: Why is it important to gather evidence before making public decisions?
How can governments include more people in decision-making?
What are the risks of waiting too long to make a decision?
Should public money be spent on repairs or on new buildings? Why?

transfer.writing: When public facilities need improvement, some people favour immediate investment while others prefer delaying major decisions until more evidence is available. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Consider costs over time and the consequences of waiting. Write at least 250 words.
